The descendants of the legendary golden realm, who chose to find new homes among the mountains and forests after abandoning their ancient civilization. The only thing they never forsook was their faith in the "Moon Goddess." However, with the arrival of the Fatui, it appears that their tranquil lives are about to fade into the realm of yesterday...
Frostmoon Scions

More than six thousand years ago, the golden kingdom of Hyperborea was destroyed, and dark blue crystal nails annihilated every last city, with even the most minuscule sign of life. Those who survived by the grace of being nowhere near the cities at the time could only cling to life amidst the freezing wind and snow. With no refuge left to them, they simply waited for destruction to find them in the hollow dark. Only the Frost Moon Goddess, Canon, answered their pleas. According to legend, she spun gleaming threads from the silver glow to lead the displaced across the frozen plains, and where her tears, full of longing, fell upon the frost-covered soil of the far north, they blossomed into lilies that would stand eternal in the icy winds. The proud descendants of Hyperborea called themselves the Frostmoon Scions, in honor of the divinity who gave humanity new life. Canon led the people to the south, to the islands that appeared from the remnants that failed to become a moon.

The Hyperboreans left the Frostmoon Scions with several devices. The only supremely advanced device was the Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb, later known as the Sampo Mill. It was designed to reconstruct matter at the subatomic scale, that is, or to transmute matter directly into stable energy. Although its structure remained largely intact, the device was unusable because the collaborative control module connected to the device was lost during the fall of Hyperborea and couldn't be replicated with existing technologies. Following the discussion, it was decided to seal the device indefinitely without re-evaluating its feasibility. The SAMPO gradually transformed from a device into a religious symbol. The Frostmoon Scions also continued the
of the Hyperborean era to create people who could wield elements. Since the core processes were lost during the fall of Hyperborea, it was decided to purify the blood of the Frostmoon Scions through controlled selection. The Frostmoon Scions believed that only the heir foretold in the prophecy could awaken the Mill and create an Elysium of eternal abundance for them. A low-tier device, created during the Hyperborean era and preserved to this day, is the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. This device is designed to solidify the Light Realm into a semi-crystalline polymeric form, which was then subjected to high frequencies with spiral acceleration, thereby purging a designated area of the Void Realm contamination. Unlike the Sampo Mill, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas could be restored and reused.

More than five hundred years ago, an outsider named Lovia, who was adopted by the previous Archpriestess, became a new leader of the Frostmoon Scions. First, she believed that they should follow the "right" path: to give grain to the hungry and tend the sick through the long night, mend the wounds of suspicion with sincerity and understanding, and soothe the troubled hearts of one's kin. When her sworn younger sister, the one with the purest blood, shielded Lovia from the traitor's blade, she realized that her gentle kindness was an unforgivable lie and established absolute power. According to prophecy, the daughter of Lovia's younger sister was to bear a sacred heir destined to rule Elysium. But when the girl met a young man from the northern kingdom, she abandoned her mission for love. She wanted her unborn son, Avrelian, to live in peace and joy, never to set foot on the lands of Nod-Krai or believe in dreams of "Elysium." Dreaming of creating an "Elysium," the Archpriestess Lovia allied herself with the Belyi Tsar's favorite, the mad monk, Rotwang. One day, he saw a pitch-black Elysium and desired to attain it. When Rotwang sent spies to capture the blessed maiden and return her to the homeland, the girl saw her lover's blood spilling beneath her feet and slit her throat. Lovia then turned to a lesser branch of the bloodline for spares, but the twin sisters, Aila and Alia, born into this family, were pale shadows of the maiden they were destined to replace. This meant that hundreds of years might pass before a child of sufficient purity would be born, and Lovia was not prepared to wait. To purify the sisters' blood, she began feeding them the blood of the Frostmoon Scions. The Archpriestess was unaware that the blessed maiden had given birth to a son, Avrelian, who, according to prophecy, would lead to Elysium. Avrelian later returned to Nod-Krai and became the great thief Reed Miller. Aila and Alia never saw their parents, and for them, only grandmother Lovia existed. The sisters hoped to one day leave this place together and see the world, but the elder, Alia, fled Hiisi Island with Avrelian when he went to the Frostmoon Scions to retrieve the Sampo Mill at the request of Professor Rotwang.

When a man named Solovei arrived on Hiisi Island, thwarting Rotwang and Lovia's plans, the Archpriestess tried to convince Aila to use her wisdom to lure him to the sanctuary and pierce his heart from behind with a sword. But Aila realized the Archpriestess had deceived her and stabbed her with a blade of pure silver. Lovia was never able to understand the reason for this betrayal. Due to the purification of her blood, Aila foresaw that decades later, a new moon goddess would be born, and everything Lovia had so long and desperately sought would be in vain. Aila had to prepare the Frostmoon Scions for the birth of the goddess and change their beliefs. After becoming the first Moonchanter, she sealed the Court of the First Edict, rewrote the old prayers, hymns, and doctrines of the Frostmoon Scions, and consigned the name of Lovia to oblivion. When
struck Teyvat five hundred years ago, the court of the Belyi Tsar could no longer mind the remote borderlands beyond the snowy plains. To combat the forces of the Abyss and the Wild Hunt, Aila, the Moonchanter, shared with Solovei, whom she saw as a hero destined to protect Elysium, the sacred relic of the Frostmoon Scions, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas. Borrowing the priestess's power, Solovei banished the darkness. Since Aila had the ability to see the future, she foresaw Rotwang's return, and Solovei decided to found an order that would meet the threat with Hyperborean technology. <color=#ffffffd9>"Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down... And at last shall he be laid to rest by the heroes of the sublunary sphere..."</color>

customize.text: Spirit Envoy Championship

When the Frostmoon Scions announced the international Spirit Envoy Championship on Hiisi Island, many candidates from various countries applied. The Traveler and Paimon were interested in the tournament but couldn't decide on a companion, as the rules stipulated that only the most common animals or their varieties could participate. Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild advised them to contact the Guild Advisor, Linnea, who possessed extensive knowledge of various creatures. Linnea also planned to participate in the competition with her companion, Lumi, a unique Jack Frost from the snow tundra. When they first met, Lumi wore a strange cardboard outfit, splattered with paint, as if she were trying to disguise herself as a common Jack Frost. The local Jack Frosts would form a pack and hound her simply for her distinctive appearance, taking all her supplies and chasing her away from her bed. Lumi couldn't deal with them and had nowhere to go, so she collected discarded cardboard boxes, painted them blue, and put them on her head, hoping to blend in among her kin. If they noticed her, she was beaten, and Lumi lived in constant fear. One day, Linnea and Lumi hid from the rain in a cave, and Lumi clung to her and refused to let go. From then on, they were inseparable, understanding each other without words. Since bonding with other creatures took a tremendous amount of time, Linnea advised pairing only with already-friendly companions in the tournament, and Aguara, a little Tepetlisaurus of the Traveler and Paimon, volunteered to participate. They discovered Aguara while he was still in hibernation on an abandoned island near Ochkanatlan. After heating the egg with phlogiston to awaken it, the Traveler and Paimon took it with them, and soon a Tepetlisaurus hatched from the egg and continued following them.

After the Traveler and Paimon had chosen a partner, Linnea escorted them to the Frostmoon Enclave to register as participants, where they met their friends. Mualani, the heroine of the People of the Springs, arrived from Natlan for the tournament, along with her Koholasaurus, Mamala. Arataki Gang's boss, Itto, arrived from Inazuma, along with the beetle, Crimson Staff. Although the gang only had enough money to send Itto alone, he hoped to use the prize money to take the other gang members to Nod-Krai. Last year's champion, Jahoda from the Curatorium of Secrets, also joined the competition, along with the Chic Badger, Reed Miller XIII. Due to the large number of applications, the tournament organizers decided to hold qualifying rounds to determine the sixteen competitors who would advance to the main tournament. Prior to the semifinals, all pairings were determined by lottery, and competitors were assigned to two arenas at random. In the qualifying round, the Traveler and Aguara were paired against Itto and Crimson Staff, while Linnea was assigned to the second arena. During the fight, Itto decided to summon his bull, Ushi, to attack Aguara together with Crimson Staff, but was disqualified for entering the arena with an extra partner. Linnea also won her round, seemingly anticipating certain moves by her opponent. During Linnea's fight, the Traveler noticed an unfamiliar girl who seemed to be following her.

After winning the qualifiers, Linnea invited the Traveler and Paimon to dine together. When Linnea was little, she noticed two unusual wings on her head, resembling unruly hair. She always felt different from everyone else, and one day she read a legend about "changelings." They say that some Fae from the tundra steal human children, leaving changelings in their place, and the humans raise the Fae's child instead of their own. The legend seemed more like a horror story for naughty children, so Linnea initially dismissed it, but then she began to notice more and more traits unique to Fae in herself. Wings began to grow on his head, and crystals appeared on his skin. At first, the girl tried to hide it, but then she decided to tell her parents. They didn't immediately believe her, but then decided to travel north to find their own child, leaving Linnea only a little money as a parting gift. After this, Linnea joined the Conch Gang, an organization of orphans living in Speranza. She eventually became the gang's boss, but had to leave due to her age. In her dreams, Linnea often heard a song in the Fae language, and she felt as if her real family didn't want to be found. Despite this, the adventurer still ventured into the tundra, where she felt very uneasy, and upon her return, she began to feel as if she was seeing certain events in advance. After dinner, Linnea invited the Traveler and Paimon to a joint training session with Lumi and Aguara to prepare for the next stages, and during the training, Linnea couldn't predict a single move the Traveler made.

The next day, the Traveler and Aguara were drawn against their old friend, the animal tamer Haniyyah from Sumeru, who participated with her Sumpter Beast, Fluffy the Flower King. Although Fluffy the Flower King was significantly larger than Aguara, the Tepetlisaurus managed to prevail. In the quarterfinals, Aguara faced Koholasaurus Mamala and, taking advantage of her blindness in one eye, managed to deliver the decisive blow, advancing to the semifinals. Linnea also advanced to the next round, and the final elimination battle was between the previous champion, Jahoda, and the mysterious girl Celaeno, who had been watching Linnea. Despite Reed Miller XIII's best efforts, Celaeno reacted very quickly to every attack, as if she had anticipated it. When Celaeno and her partner, the Radiant Bladehorn Haemus, won, the girl's hat flew off, revealing wings identical to Linnea's. The Guild Advisor tried to ask the girl who she was, but grabbed her hand and lost consciousness. Opening her eyes, Linnea found herself in a dream in which she was to fight Celaeno and Haemus in the semifinals, but when she opened her eyes again, Celaeno had already won. In the next moments, the girl saw her future life: how she completed commissions to save up for her own ship, how she set off on a journey on that ship, how the ship crashed, how she met Celaeno to say goodbye to their parents, and how her life ended.

When Linnea awoke from this dream and told the Traveler and Paimon what had happened, they suggested they ask Celaeno for answers. Aguara discovered the girl's trail and led them to The Flagship. Although she was reluctant to speak with Linnea, the Guild Advisor did not give up until she opened the door. Celaeno explained that she and Linnea were sisters and belonged to a rare species of Fae, Augury Birds, able to see the key points of their fate. They knew in advance what troubles and joys awaited them, but were powerless to change anything. And in the end, only callousness and emptiness remained in their souls. It was believed that if an Augury Bird grew up far from the Fae, among humans, their ability to foresee would awaken much later, so Linnea's parents swapped the human girl for their own daughter. The girl was born with a rare disease that humans cannot cure, and without the switch, she would have died. Celaeno had envied her sister's life all her life, having discovered her abilities many years ago. When she and her parents visited Linnea, she imagined her life to be perfect, and she hoped to find her when she grew up and tell her everything, so that her sister would feel the same pain. But when Celaeno overheard Linnea talking about how she was abandoned by her adoptive parents, she realized that the happy Linnea, her parents' favorite, and the girl favored by fate, was in fact just a figment of her imagination. In reality, she didn't envy her sister, but she was lonely and longed for a family. Linnea didn't resent her older sister and was happy to finally meet her family.

Although Linnea had foreseen her defeat in the semifinals, she wasn't ready to give in to fate and went to training with Lumi, where she met up with the Traveler, Paimon, and Aguara. The next day, in the semifinals, Aguara faced a Snegurochka from Snezhnaya, Viliana, and the snow fox, Gorynishche, but after a night of training, he easily won the duel. In the battle between Lumi and Haemus, Celaeno predicted every move, but Lumi suddenly absorbed a large amount of Geo, increasing her size tenfold. But as she was about to deliver the finishing blow to Haemus and Celaeno, Linnea pulled her back to save her sister. At the very moment the hammer began to descend, the future Celaeno had envisioned was replaced by a complete void. Linnea may have momentarily defeated fate, but ultimately, her decision still led to a predetermined outcome. However, Linnea was not upset by her defeat or the inevitability of fate, for although there is only one destination, there are countless paths leading to it.

To prepare Aguara for the final battle with Haemus, Linnea suggested traveling to the Tepetlisaurus's homeland of Natlan and restoring his strength with phlogiston. Since both Lumi and Aguara used Geo, Linnea asked her Jack Frost to teach him the technique of creating a stone hammer from Geo. Although the Tepetlisaurus struggled to learn, that night, when everyone had gone to bed, the Traveler and Paimon's Saurian companion, Little One, came to his aid and taught him the proper technique. During the final battle, Aguara used the Geo weapon and crushed Haemus, winning the Spirit Envoy Championship. After the tournament, Celaeno released Haemus to Hiisi Island.

customize.text: Frostmoon Enclave

The Frostmoon Enclave is home to the indigenous inhabitants of Nod-Krai, the Frostmoon Scions, who settled on Hiisi Island around six thousand years ago. Over five hundred years ago, their home was enclosed by a golden wall, through which no one and nothing could penetrate, but now the Frostmoon Scions are open to all. The first to change the Frostmoon Scions' ways was the first Moonchanter, Aila, and now the current Moonchanter, Lauma, who both revealed the truth about the true moon to the people. When the Traveler and Paimon first traveled to Hiisi Island to visit the Frostmoon Scions, a strong wind suddenly blew at the entrance to the Frostmoon Enclave, and then the flower petals transformed into a strange kuuhenki, Luonnotar, a creature said to be born with the blessing of the Moon Goddess. According to legend, the Luonnotar brings good luck, so the Traveler and Paimon allowed it to accompany them on their journey. In truth, the Luonnotar was a fragment of the Moon Goddess Columbina's soul, an anchor she left behind from the future in the past to return to Teyvat from the moon's reflection. When Columbina was able to return from the prison, the Luonnotar merged with her, but the Moon Goddess later created a new Luonnotar, imbuing it with the memories of all their past adventures with the Traveler.

At the entrance to the Frostmoon Enclave stands a statue of the Moon Goddess, built by the first generation of Frostmoon Scions to settle on the island around six thousand years ago. Similar statues were built throughout Nod-Krai and crafted from the very finest Lunasoul Stone. This stone was not only extremely rare but also infused with kuuvahki. When the Fatui pulled several fragments of Ancient Moon's Remnants down in Nod-Krai, one fell on Hiisi Island. The Fatui first began modifying and defacing the Moon Goddess statues throughout Nod-Krai, then set out to seize the last statue in the Frostmoon Enclave and its fragment of Ancient Moon's Remnants. The Moonchanter, Lauma, refused to give up the fragments to the Fatui, even under threat of attack, and promised that if they set foot on their land with ill intent, their blood would be the border. After the Fatui had repeatedly teamed up with the Frostmoon Scions to save Nod-Krai from the Sinner, Rerir, who was trying to seize the power of kuuvahki, to retrieve the Moon Goddess, and then save Nod-Krai from the Harbinger Dottore, Harbinger Marionette invited the Moonchanter to a tea party, where she brewed herbal tea according to the traditions of the Frostmoon Scions as a sign of respect and promised not to hinder them anymore.

Throughout the Frostmoon Enclave, Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms, associated with the Moon Goddess, Kuutar, grow everywhere. By their changing patterns, the Frostmoon Scions determine the approach of Moon-Prayer Night, a traditional holiday of the Frostmoon Scions in honor of the birth of the Moon Goddess. The holiday has no fixed date and depends on the movement of the moon, as Moon-Prayer Night is when the moon is closest to Teyvat. As the moon approaches, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon, and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance, considered a blessed omen. When the Frostmoon Scions learned that their beliefs were false, Moon-Prayer Night became more of a local custom than a celebration of the Moon Goddess, and has evolved into the most popular holiday in Nod-Krai, celebrated even by ordinary people. Traditionally, the Frostmoon Scions decorated themselves and their settlement with the Moon-Prayer Blossoms, sang and danced, and shared food and handicrafts with all guests. When the festival spread beyond Hiisi Island to Nasha Town, people began decorating the town for the festival, and the best Frostmoon Scions' artisans sculpted a deer statue that graced the town square.

When the Moonchanter, Lauma, was born, the people exclaimed, <color=#ffffffd9>"Behold: eyes like the moonlit tide, antlers like the crescent moon, and blood that glimmers silver as the moon's reflection..."</color> For many years, the blood of the Frostmoon Scions had been fading, so large antlers like Lauma's were rarely seen more than once every hundred years. In a cave beneath Hiisi Island, there is a special tree whose branches, like Lauma's antlers, respond to the tides of kuuvahki. She was incredibly sensitive to Moon Marrow and kuuvahki’s ebb and flow. For others, the fluctuations of kuuvahki were like a gentle tide lapping away at the shore, but for her, it was a massive tsunami crashing over her body. From birth, she was revered as the Messenger of the "Frostmoon's Emissary" and the "Moon-Tide Maiden," and the first words she learned were prayers to the Frost Moon. Her first gestures were those of sacred rituals. From the moment she was first taught to pray, those closest to her would point to the night sky and say, <color=#ffffffd9>"That, Lauma, is the Frostmoon — the last of the moons, the sole surviving truth."</color> But she felt nothing from it, and later realized that people simply couldn't determine where the tide actually came from, nor did they sense the real Moon, hidden behind the veil of the sky. She had long since realized that the Moon in the sky was not real, but she couldn't tell a single soul this and chose the path of concealment. Lauma knew too much, so she was forced to keep her loved ones in the dark, and every prayer she uttered seemed like a lie to her, but it helped her to live on. Only with time, when the Moon Goddess, Kuutar, had already returned to Hiisi Island, was Lauma able to reveal the truth about the real Moon to the Frostmoon Scions. Some were unable to accept this and left the island forever, while others began to learn to live with the new truth.

Lauma also possesses the ability to understand and communicate with animals. While this often helps her learn about events in Nod-Krai or deliver messages quickly, it can often be unbearable. Since Lauma cannot control her ability, she cannot enjoy the birdsong deep in the forest. Instead of peace and tranquility, she hears arguments about who destroyed whose nest or which part of the forest contains the best twigs. Because ordinary people cannot understand animal speech and behavior, many works on this topic use the phrase "bestial nature" with a negative connotation, while "human nature" is explored in a multifaceted manner. But for Lauma, both "human nature" and "bestial nature" are simply "nature," and everyone has their moments of courage and cowardice, greed and rage. Both humans and animals rejoice in success and mourn failure, so the Moonchanter wishes for animals and humans to communicate freely. One day, the Traveler, Paimon, and the Moon Goddess wanted to ask Lauma to help a Chic Badger whose home was being attacked by monsters. While they waited for the right moment to approach the Moonchanter unnoticed, they saw how much she did for both humans and animals, constantly helping them.

One day, a Weasel Thief and an ibis offered to help Lauma retrieve the Lunar Semblance, sealed in the Moon Mirror by the previous Moonchanter. The statue's value lay in the stories associated with it, and Moonchanter hoped to find these stories, verify them, and share them with everyone. The Weasel Thief had conducted reconnaissance beforehand and discovered that the seal contained no deadly traps, then demanded payment for her assistance. The Traveler and Paimon helped Lauma remove the seal from the Moon Mirror, as pairs of mechanisms had to be activated simultaneously in two different locations. The ibis in the sky informed Lauma of their location and the mechanism before them.

Once the Lunar Semblance statue was retrieved, the animals delivered it to the Frostmoon Scions' library, which Lauma had restored. The Moonchanter also asked the Traveler to bring her texts about the Frostmoon Scions to expand her library. After the Weasel Thief helped her obtain the statue, he wanted to join the Traveler on their journey to open all the treasure chests in the world. He even gave the Traveler a Mora coin as a token of the agreement between him and the Weasel Thieves. And if they ever became interested in the offer, all they had to do was leave some dried Lakkaberries near their pillow. After finding the Lunar Semblance, the little Weasel Thief's passion only grew, and it constantly began asking Lauma about finding new treasures. Then the Weasel Thief began digging up anything it thought valuable and bringing it to her library. Thus, the library accumulated entire deposits of petrified seeds of an ancient tree, fossilized animal bones, colorful stones, Mora deposit boxes that people buried for safekeeping, wish-boxes, letters with enclosed photographs, and much more. To avoid breaking the heart of the little Weasel Thief who had given these gifts, Lauma asked another Weasel to return the stolen items to their proper place, and sorted the rest into categories.

In the library, Priestess Ehrnrooth, recording the hymns of the Frostmoon Scions, can be found. During her tenure as priestess, she learned many stories to record. For example, one of the previous Moonchanters had a strange habit of spending two hours soaking in a nearby lake whenever she had to organize some ceremony, regardless of the season. She would say that the lake reflected the moon, and that she could enjoy the favor of its light and goddess while thus immersed, which would then help the ceremony proceed smoothly. In times when a great many ceremonies were held, she would be soaking practically every day, and the constant cold caused her severe arthritis, forcing her to retire early. Despite her premature retirement, she claimed the pain was a sign of the Moon Goddess's regard, as the moon would be covered by the clouds and disappear when it would rain, as if bidding farewell. Later, in her old age, the Frostmoon Scions had to find her an acolyte to watch her permanently and ensure that she did not risk her health further. That servant turned out to be Ehrnrooth, who had learned much from the Moonchanter and dreamed of publishing the stories she told as a book. When the current Moonchanter, Lauma, learned of Ehrnrooth's book, she approved of the idea and suggested calling it "Lost Tales of the Moonchanters."

One day, a legal consultant from Liyue with Adeptal blood in her veins, Yanfei, visited the Frostmoon Scions' library. Like Lauma, she had antlers growing on her head, which fascinated the local children. Yanfei asked to see some data and materials and promised to send them some books on the "boundaries of law" in exchange, explaining issues of law, right, and legal norms in various countries. Yanfei also told Lauma the legends of Liyue and the legend of the White Horse Adeptus, who had a strong connection with the Moon. The books of the Frostmoon Scions also spoke of a deity that once lived on the surface of the Moon.

One day, the children, Kari and Ina, picked up an injured little puffin, and Kari wanted to keep it and befriend it, but the puffin flew away after getting better. The next day, the children saw another puffin in a tree and asked it to tell the little puffin that they missed it. Since the children couldn't communicate with animals, the Moonchanter came to their aid. The bird explained that the little puffin had been locked in the house and was being scolded by its parents for being away too long, but it also longed to see them. Then the other puffin and a deer escorted the children to their friend's home so they could meet, and Lauma, in gratitude, prepared sweet fruits for them in the library. When the children followed the deer and found themselves in a forest filled with dead ends, one suddenly sat on Kari's head, then crawled into his pocket and began spinning like a top, and the boy immediately recognized it as the puffin he had saved. After the children had played enough with the birds, the deer led them home so they wouldn't get lost.

In addition to the ability to speak with animals, the Moonchanter also possesses healing blood. She keeps this ability a secret, but she has used this method of healing many times, and her hands are covered in cuts, as many Frostmoon Scions distrust medicine from the Snezhnaya. One of the followers Lauma cured was a girl, Kaarina, who had fallen ill from the influence of the kuuvahki. Lauma's blood could neutralize the kuuvahki's influence on ordinary people, but a full cure still required medicine, which the Moonchanter requested from the Curatorium of Secrets. Besides Kaarina, Lauma used her blood to heal the eyes of the Curatorium of Secrets boss, Nefer, who was injured during a fight with the Rächer of Solnari.

Not far from the library, Mirsky, a mechanic from Nasha Town who is in love with Verna, a priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, can be met. They are both fascinated by mechanisms and sometimes meet to discuss various technical matters. Mirsky decided to learn the prayers of the Frostmoon Scions so that he and Verna could pray together. He also offered to install an automatic water pump, support pillars to strengthen houses, sewing machines, and make jumping frogs for children for the Moonchanter. In exchange for payment, the mechanic wanted permission to visit the library and study kuuvahki. Besides Mirsky, another Nasha Town resident in the Enclave, the carpenter Wecksell, can be met. The Frostmoon Scions once helped him, so he felt obligated and began repairing the house to pay for their help. The priestesses invited him to join the Frostmoon Scions and officially settle there, but he declined, as he didn't believe in the gods and didn't want to cause trouble. The Moonchanter, upon learning of the offer, assured Wecksell that the question of faith would not cause any concern, as he was already a member of their family.

In the caves beneath the Frostmoon Enclave, where the Frostmoon Scions left their Moon Mirrors, dwells the Tsar Crab, a mutated lord of the crabs whose mind, infected by ancient Moon Marrow, was temporarily consumed by madness. Believed to be several hundred years old, its home is an unusual shell, a huge, mountain-like structure covered in kuuvahki-filled moss. In the darkness of the cave, this moss glows like a scattering of tiny stars. Crabs around Hiisi Island often bring the Tsar Crab Lakkaberries, fish, Moonfall Silver, and other materials. According to legend, hidden in the depths of the Tsar Crab's palace is a most precious treasure,
of manipulating human desires. According to legend, the Frostmoon Scions' Archpriestess, Lovia, was also bewitched by such a stone of desire five hundred years ago, and Aila convinced the great thief Reed Miller to steal it. In reality, the stone of desire is a fragment from the orbital positioning
that recently fell on Hiisi Island. Under the influence of this fragment, the Tsar Crab learned to pass through the mirrors of the Frostmoon Scions and transformed into an evil, cruel, and hot-tempered crab, even occasionally attacking smaller crabs. The self-proclaimed heir of the great thief, Maite Veliu of the Conch Gang, set out to retrieve the Tsar Crab's treasure. The con artist Hidimbi from Sumeru told her about the wishing stone and promised to sell it for a high price. When the Traveler and Paimon teamed up with Maite to retrieve this fragment, they encountered a strange priestess in a mirror reflection along the way. She recognized the Traveler as the Ruler of "Elysium" and directed them to the fragment of the "Engraving." After defeating the Tsar Crab, the fragment returned to the main "Engraving" above the Court of the First Edict, and the Tsar Crab itself finally calmed down and stopped attacking everyone around it.

One day, while wandering through the Frostmoon Enclave, the Traveler and Paimon met the daughter of the priestess Rahetar, Kasha, who was searching for beautiful stones to bribe a friend from Nasha Town. Kasha had heard a legend about a great thief and a Fae princess, in which Reed Miller charmed the princess's heart with a gem and lured her from a gilded cage. So Kasha decided that her friend would join her on their journey if she gave her a gift. The stone Kasha was searching for turned out to be one of the fragments of the ancient dragons' orbital positioning facility, and when they retrieved it, it became drawn to a huge boulder in the center of the Enclave. After the Traveler returned the stone, the boulder suddenly rose from the ground and connected with the Engraving above the Court of the First Edict. Although Kasha couldn't bribe her friend with the beautiful stone, she now had a story to tell about the floating stone. To the right of the Enclave lies a hidden trove, which can be opened with three Evermoon Seals.

On the coast of Hiisi Island, the Traveler and Paimon once encountered the best fisherman of the Frostmoon Scions, Pekkani. Pekkani hadn't been able to catch a single fish, so he asked the adventurers to study the local waters and find out what exactly was stopping the fish from biting. Three fragments of a boulder lying nearby were discovered in the water near the fisherman. After the Traveler returned all three stones to their original position, the boulder rose and merged with the Engraving. Icy pebbles can be found all along the coast of Hiisi Island. According to ancient legend, this hole once served as a refuge to which the Frost Moon led the Fae, as well as a gateway to the ethereal. In another story popular in Nasha Town, the legendary thief, Reed Miller, was surrounded when a runestone given to him by a holy lady of the Frost Moon as a token of her love allowed him to conceal himself and escape his pursuers, but the Frostmoon Scions themselves claim this is a myth. One day, the naturalist explorer, Linnea of ​​the Adventurers' Guild, went in search of the icy pebbles and met her friend from the Conch Gang, Auni, and a man named Viljami. He told how, once upon a time, during his years of wandering the seas, he heard a calling coming from nowhere. The others didn't respond, but he fell under its spell almost instantly. Only later did he realize that this call carried within it all the dreams that were never destined to reach the distant shore, a collection of regrets. Then he recklessly rushed forward, because even danger seemed like an opportunity, but the sea and its furious winds took everything from him: wealth, honor, and even family. Auni suggested that Viljami should have looked through a hole in the icy pebble to see who was calling him, and while searching for the entrance to ethereal, her head got stuck through the hole, forcing Linnea to help her.

When the Rächer of Solnari attacked Nod-Krai and the Moon Goddess, she was too weak to fight him. To regain her strength, she asked her former colleague, the Harbinger Arlecchino, to locate the Iridescent Moon Marrow. Arlecchino was the heir to the blood of the Crimson Moon dynasty, and the ancient Balemoon Bloodfire flowed through her veins. The Crimson Moon was, in truth, the Iridescent Moon, merging with the Abyss to survive the War of Funerary Flame. When Arlecchino first became a Harbinger, the Director of the Fatui Harbingers gave her a book which claimed that in the Crimson Moon era, there was an orphanage that received children from beyond the bounds of this world and subjected them to a peculiar induction ceremony. The Crimson Moon sages looked beyond this world for beings with powers that surpassed the gods — but, fearing they might lose control, they subjected these children to a process of "refinement." They made these children crawl up a fireplace and kept asking them, <color=#ffffffd9>"Have you died?" "Did you see it?"</color> until they finally admitted to having died and seen a crimson moon. The adults embraced the children who passed the ritual, telling them, <color=#ffffffd9>"Within the fireplace, you have traversed the flames between two worlds. Here and now, you are born anew."</color> Arlecchino suspected that this was their way of "branding" the children they had enrolled — leaving an indelible mark upon them so that they would forever live in the Crimson Moon's light. And the Iridescent Moon's Marrow was sealed in a special space that could only be accessed temporarily through some kind of ritual. The chimney and fireplace were merely formalities in the ritual, and the key was crossing "the flames between two worlds" — the flames that burn within the Harbinger. On the western coast of the Frostmoon Enclave, Arlecchino opened a portal leading to the space of the Crimson Moon so that Columbina could receive its power. Moreover, this same location was the site of the battle between the Moon Goddess and her friends against the Rächer of Solnari, during which they were able to send the Sinner into the moon's reflection.

To the west of the Frostmoon Enclave is the site of the "Spirit Envoy Championship," an animal tournament. The Frostmoon Scions have always advocated coexistence with nature, encouraging their followers to build positive relationships with the beasts of the wild. At the same time, to ensure their animal friends build the strength to withstand hardship and disasters, they put selected animals with whom they share a special bond through a unique sort of training. The Spirit Envoy Championship is designed to determine the strongest human-animal pair among all the tournament participants. In previous years, the competition was restricted to the Frostmoon Scions only, but in the last year, participants from all over the world were invited to participate. The Traveler and Paimon also decided to participate with their Tepetlisaurus, Aguara, whom they found as an egg in Ochkanatlan. Friends from all over the world also arrived for the tournament: Mualani from Natlan with the Koholasaurus, Mamala, Arataki Itto from Inazuma with the beetle, Crimson Staff, Haniyyah from Sumeru with the Sumpter Beast, Fluffy the Flower King, and the Adventurer's Guild advisor Linnea with the Jack Frost, Lumi. Guests from Snezhnaya also arrived for the Spirit Envoy Championship: the Snegurochka Viliana with the fox, Gorynishche, and the Augury Bird Celaeno with the Radiant Bladehorn, Haemus. Thanks to the help of their Tepetlisaurus companion, Little One, who taught Aguara how to harness the power of phlogiston, the Traveler defeated Celaeno in the tournament finals and became the winner of the Spirit Envoy Championship. Celaeno met the Radiant Bladehorn in Nod-Krai as a cub when she came with her parents to visit her sister. Haemus had lost its parents, so she took it under her wing and raised it in Snezhnaya. After the tournament, Celaeno released Haemus into the wild on Hiisi Island so it could live freely.

customize.text: Light-Bathed Platform

Near the Frostmoon Enclave is located the Light-Bathed Platform where a statue of the Moon Goddess
stands. When the Moon Goddess was born on Hiisi Island nearly five hundred years ago, the moment of her birth was witnessed by the first Moonchanter, Aila. She recognized this as the prophesied rebirth of the Frostmoon Goddess and carved a statue in honor of the miracle that had occurred, in the likeness of Kuutar at the moment of her birth. It was here that the Frostmoon Scions left offerings to Kuutar and asked for her aid. When they were transformed by the current Moonchanter, Lauma, Columbina returned to them once again, not as their goddess, but as a member of their family. After Kuutar attained the Trilunar authority and gained her wings, the Frostmoon Scions added these wings to the statue in honor of their goddess's ability to soar once again, her fingers finally touching the place called "home." Columbina previously felt a sense of confusion when looking at this statue, but now, after her rebirth, she feels the warmth of "home."

Standing before the statue of the Moon Goddess is the entrance to the Frostmoon Scions' sanctuary, where the sacred relic known as the Eternal Moon Marrow was safeguarded for generations. Blessed with the power of the goddess Aria, the Eternal Moon Marrow possesses the ability to reveal the true past. Only the Archpriestess and the Moonchanters could use this relic once a year, on the Moon-Prayer Night, when the kuuvahki of Nod-Krai reached its peak. The Traveler wanted to use the Moon Marrow to learn the truth about their arrival in Teyvat on the ship that had ended up in Nod-Krai, but the Moon-Prayer Night was still two months away. One night, they decided to go for a walk after being unable to sleep due to obsessive thoughts about their ship, the Moon Marrow, and their twin. On Hiisi Island, they suddenly saw their twin's silhouette in the distance. When the Traveler finally caught up with their sibling, it turned out that they, too, were interested in the sacred relic of the Frostmoon Scions for answers about their past and the origin of Teyvat, but weren't willing to wait two months for its reveal. They decided to use the power of the Abyss to infiltrate the sanctuary. Although the Traveler was hesitant to use the relic without Lauma's permission, they followed their twin anyway.

Trials awaited them inside, which they were able to overcome using a combination of kuuvahki and Abyssal energy. When they overcame all obstacles and penetrated the heart of the sanctuary, their twin suddenly ordered the Traveler to bring the Moon Marrow. The Traveler suspected something was wrong, but while they hesitated, a fog spread around them, and their sibling vanished along with the relic, while the Traveler lost consciousness. When they finally woke up, they were already outside the sanctuary, and the Wild Hunt, one of the Abyssal manifestations in Nod-Krai, was closing in. Ratnik Flins, patrolling the grounds, came to their aid. Although the Traveler suspected that the twin had stolen the relic, there was actually a third person involved. One of the priestesses of the Frostmoon Scions, Vilemina, had become disillusioned with them, believing them to be stubborn and stuck in their ways, clinging to a "truth" they didn't even question. Some time ago, she secretly joined the Fatui. At first, they didn't accept her, but Harbinger Sandrone noticed her and decided to give her a chance. Marionette instructed the girl to follow the Traveler, and when she saw the Traveler and their twin enter the sanctuary, she decided to steal the Moon Marrow herself, so that it would serve as a way to the Fatui. Since Sandrone had not given the order to seize the Frostmoon Scions' relic, she later returned it to Lauma, and the Traveler suggested Lauma try concealing the Moon Marrow within their body, preventing either the Fatui or the Wild Hunt from reaching it. Due to the unique constitution of the Descender's body, the Moon Marrow did not cause them any harm, but only strengthened their connection with the kuuvahki.

Near Hiisi Island lies Thunderclap Reef, an island affected by kuuvahki disturbances. For nearly five hundred years, kuuvahki on Thunderclap Reef had always been unstable, but after two stones fell from the sky, the situation worsened. On the island, the Traveler and Paimon met a woman in a kuuvahki-protective suit who introduced herself as a "servant of the Frost Moon, born of the tides, and bearer of the High Priestess's mantle beneath the moon's silver gaze, known in the sublunary sphere as
Although the Traveler and Paimon believed her to be an impostor posing as a priestess, they agreed to help her resolve the disturbance. Since Verna had studied under the renowned mechanic Papa Wrench, she calculated that the two stones causing the disturbance were imbued with powerful kuuvahki energy, which had upset the island's balance. To eliminate the disturbance, it was necessary to find other fragments imbued with kuuvahki and strike them against these stones at the correct angle. Verna attempted to find the fragments using her robots, Kraka V and Kraka VII, but they never returned, and the priestess herself was unable to enter due to the dangerous influence of the kuuvahki. Since the Traveler and Paimon were not affected by the kuuvahki, they set out to find the robot and stone fragments. When they collected a fragment and threw it at the stone, the cave entrance collapsed, blocking the exit, and the other fragment only intensified the kuuvahki disturbance on the island, reversing it. Verna calculated that the third fragment would stabilize the kuuvahki, and one of her robots detected the kuuvahki signal, which led the Traveler, Paimon, and Verna to the Moon Mirrors, where they again saw the mysterious priestess instructing them. Although Verna believed the priestess to be a fraud, the latter led them to the final stone fragment and promised to wait for them in the Court of the First Edict. When they threw the final fragment into the stones, the anomaly on the island was eliminated, and the stones returned to the Engraving above the Court of the First Edict.
Due to the kuuvahki disturbances, a purple Chic Badger appeared in the Thunderclap Reef region, its mane changing color under the influence of the kuuvahki. Naturalist Linnea, who studies the world, became intrigued by this unusual Chic Badger and decided to find it to study and record a strange animal in her encyclopedia.

Across the ravine beyond the Moon Goddess's statue lies the Court of the First Edict, and above it rises a stone Engraving. This Engraving, an orbital positioning facility, was built by the ancient dragon Moongazer Ibni-Belum in
several millennia ago, before the Heavenly Principles had yet emerged in Teyvat. This redundant node was built to enhance the overall structural robustness and fault-tolerance threshold of the Frost Moon storage array. In the event of unforeseen, extreme circumstances, including physical destruction and cognitive contamination that could lead to irreversible damage to the primary lunar storage array, subsequent researchers would retain access to the backup storage array located in Nephilheim, ensuring the lossless retrieval and recovery of core research results. While not the original design intent, the facility could also serve as an emergency bunker. It was near the ancient dragons' backup database that the Moon Goddess, Kuutar, was reborn. The upper portion of the Engraving had recently fallen from the sky, and several fragments had broken off. Two fragments fell in the Frostmoon Enclave, one landed on the island's coast, and the last fell in Thunderclap Reef. When the Traveler and Paimon collected the stone fragments that had fallen from the sky, they returned to their original position and attached themselves to the upper portion of the Engraving.

Beneath the stone Engraving lies the Court of the First Edict — an ancient sanctuary sealed five hundred years ago by decree of the first Moonchanter, Aila. Due to the seal placed upon it, which no one had ever been able to remove, the place became a forbidden area for the Frostmoon Scions. But when a mysterious priestess in the Moon Mirrors summoned the Traveler, Paimon, and Verna to the Court, they decided to break the seal. Verna believed the mysterious priestess intended to exploit their curiosity to remove the seal from the sanctuary and gain access to the treasures within, so she resolved to catch the impostor in the act. Although the Traveler and Paimon still considered the priestess more trustworthy than Verna herself, they agreed to infiltrate the Court of the First Edict to meet her. Verna calculated that the sanctuary, sealed by the power of the kuuvahki, could be opened in the same way as on Thunderclap Reef, and she tasked her robots with finding more similar stone fragments to break the seal. Once the fragments were collected, a Moonlane appeared before the Traveler, Verna, and Paimon, leading them to the Interstice of the Nearing Moon created by the ancient dragons. After the Traveler moved the floating columns onto the tracks, the dragons' security systems recognized them as Flamelord Xiuhcoatl and lifted the seal on the Court of the First Edict.

For several millennia, the Court of the First Edict — an emergency bunker built by the dragons — was used for all rituals of the Frostmoon Scions. The Verdant Crest growing within the sanctuary was a sacred tree that, according to legend, witnessed the birth of the
Near the tree lay an inexhaustible
blessed by the first Moonchanter, Aila. Hidden within the pool was a blade forged from the moonlight in Hyperborea by a sacred
of the far north. It was this blade that was used to sacrifice the first drop of blood to the newborn Moon Goddess, and with it, the first Moonchanter pierced the previous Archpriestess, Lovia, who was behind many crimes against the Frostmoon Scions. At that time, the
of Moon light was very weak, so many rituals failed to work properly. To maintain the rituals, Lovia committed numerous atrocities and allied herself with Rotwang from Snezhnaya. When the Traveler, Paimon, and Verna infiltrated the sanctuary, they encountered the afterimage of the mysterious priestess — the first Moonchanter, Aila. Possessing the gift of foresight, she foresaw both the fall of the stones that had fallen only months earlier and the appearance of
Their threads of fate barely intertwined with the web of the sublunary sphere, so the priestess had to guide them with stones that also did not belong to this world. Aila believed the Traveler was a hero of the sublunary sphere, the one destined to fell the
As a sign of apology, she left behind the last sword forged in moonlight and directed them to follow the light that would lead them to the one who shared her blood, to understand the meaning of the spoken words.

Although Verna had invaded the Court of the First Edict at the direction of the first Moonchanter, she was punished upon her return. The Moonchanter, Lauma, after listening to Verna, sent her to copy the hymns, and while the priestess was immersed in her work, she finally understood Aila's words. She recalled that the Moonchanter had gone to the Pillar of Embla, where she had stopped the plague of the Abyss, and guessed that the word "serpent" could be a metaphor for the Abyss. It was there that the Traveler and Paimon had gone to stop the immortal serpent.

Beyond the Court of the First Edict lies a portal leading to a sanctuary of ancient Hyperborea, where the people communed with the Moons. When the Moon Goddess vanished, having exhausted all her powers, her friends set out to search for her name, hoping to find clues in Hyperborea. Opening the portal required three people capable of achieving resonance with kuuvahki to open it. The simplest method was to extract a small amount of kuuvahki from the soil of Nod-Krai and inject it into the body. To test whether the candidates were suitable for such power, Nicole tested kuuvahki on them, and the Traveler and the Moonchanter, Lauma, passed the test. But since Grand Master Varka failed the test, they needed a third person. Nefer and Jahoda from the Curatorium of Secrets were unable to withstand kuuvahki power, while Ineffa, Aino, and Flins were unsuitable for the test. Then, Fatui Harbinger Arlecchino, who was capable of holding the Iridescent Moon Marrow within herself, came to their aid. For three days, the Traveler, Arlecchino, and Lauma were to stand motionless without food or water, while the others remained to monitor their condition. When the ritual was finally completed, Nicole was able to open a portal to the Hyperborean sanctuary. After the Moon Goddess returned, she used this sanctuary to return to the Frost Moon, but was stopped by the Harbinger Fatui Dottore.

In the very north of the island, the Frostnight Herra can be encountered. It is a proud being who roams in the waning glow of the moon and wields the powers of the Light Realm. Its rainbow wings still glow with the majesty of a primeval era. Legend has it that these graceful and mysterious beasts were created by the first emissary in the era when the Frost Moon still revolved in its orbit, and, favored by the divine emissary, they would not be tainted by the light of day. When Elysium fell, they made a pact with the mistress of the Frost Moon, vowing to use the primal light bestowed by the Frost Moon to cleanse the mortal world's defilement until the patron of old could return once more. Even now, among the followers of the Frost Moon, they are regarded as sacred beasts lost to this world, retreating along secret lunar paths beyond the reach of mortal eyes. Yet, as they have for countless centuries past, they still wander in the shadows of the moon, treading the boundary between two worlds, guarding the lands coveted by calamity, and watching over those who dwell within them — for this is the very oath they first swore to the apostle of the

South of the Court of the First Edict lies an abandoned lunar court. Three moons once shone in the sky, and the lunar people knew the secrets of the lunar phases, being able to predict the tidal ebb and flow. Whatever they gently touched with their fingers would surge with moonlit might, but then the moonlight dimmed, and the people were left to wander aimlessly, defenseless and leaderless. Legend has it that the Frostmoon Scions constructed a lunar court in the border realms, summoning lost moonlight back to them. But where reflected light once flowed through these stone carvings, there is now only frozen silence, and the secrets hidden within this silence still swirl in the labyrinth of time.

The moon-blessed land located in the northwestern regions of Teyvat.

Follow the silver thread spun by the new moon, traverse biting gales and desolate tundras as the snow-kissed lakes, fractured like mirrors, reflect their ageless, glacial radiance. The days are bitterly short, and the night stretches on like a dark, yawning maw. But even then, the light and song of the Welkin Moon will dance gently across the faces of visiting travelers. Up at ye towers, and let your lanterns blaze into the darkness! Until the day comes... when true moonlight bathes this land once more.

customize.name: Frost Moon
customize.desc: Long before the children of humanity were born from the cradle of the sky, three silver lights had already risen above the earth. The ancient spirits of the frostbound reaches called them "Dilimbabbar." By them, the waxing and waning of light were first distinguished, spring and autumn were set into order, and the passage of years slowly came to be. Yet now, as time flows ever onward, only one of those three silver lights remains.

customize.name: Elemental Dragons
customize.desc: An ancient race, who ruled Teyvat long before human existence. Dragons belong to the Light Realm.

customize.name: Frostmoon Scions
customize.desc: The descendants of the legendary golden realm, who chose to find new homes among the mountains and forests after abandoning all civilization. The only thing they never forsook was their faith in the "Moon Goddess."

customize.name: Moon Goddesses
customize.desc: Aria, Sonnet, and Canon — three sisters and Moon Goddesses who once ruled the firmament. Columbina Hyposelenia is a Moon Goddess who was born thousands of years after the Three Moon's death.

customize.name: Fatui
customize.desc: A Snezhnayan organization that is loyal to the Tsaritsa and has spread out all over the continent. Its Harbingers are on the hunt for the Gnoses.

customize.name: Aila

customize.name: Columbina

customize.name: Anacharsis
customize.desc: A voyager from the race of chroniclers who keep track of all worlds in the universe. One day, she disobeyed the cardinal rule and descended to Teyvat, leading a rebellion against the Heavenly Principles.

customize.name: Verna
customize.desc: A High Priestess of the Frosmoom Scions. Her full name is Vernadska.

customize.name: Alia
customize.desc: The second Reed Miller and the First Moonchanter's sister from the Frostmoon Scions. She lived 500 years ago.

customize.name: Nicole
customize.desc: A prophetess and a member of the Hexenzirkel. She is also known as Nicole Reeyn and N. She is one of the last angels who remained conscious. She lost her voice and can only talk inside people's heads.

customize.name: Lauma
customize.desc: A Maiden blessed by moonlight and the grove alike, hope born to the Frostmoon Scions.

customize.name: Rerir
customize.desc: One of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, also known as "Rächer of Solnari."

customize.name: Sandrone
customize.desc: The Seventh of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, codenamed Marionette. Her real name is Marionette Guillotin.

customize.name: Linnea
customize.desc: Naturalist and Advisor to the Nod-Krai Branch of the Adventurers' Guild.

customize.name: Rotwang
customize.desc: A "mad monk,' exiled from Khaenri'ah, who dreamt of the pitch-black Elysium. His real name is Rauthvangi.

customize.name: Il Dottore
customize.desc: The Second of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, codenamed The Doctor. Had multiple "segments" of himself, nearly all of which he destroyed in a deal with the Dendro Archon. His real name is Zandik.

customize.name: Frostnight Herra
customize.desc:
Proud beings that roam in the waning glow of the moon, wielding ancient powers long since tamed by the Lord of the Sky.
Legends say these graceful, mystical beasts were born in the age when the Frost Moon still turned, and, favored by the divine emissary, they would not be tainted by the light of day. Even now, among the followers of the Frost Moon, they are regarded as sacred beasts lost to this world, retreating along secret lunar paths beyond the reach of mortal eyes. Yet, as they have for countless centuries past, they still wander in the shadows of the moon, treading the boundary between two worlds, guarding the lands coveted by calamity, and watching over those who dwell within them — for this is the very oath they first swore to the apostle of the golden city.

customize.name: Moonweaver's Dawn
customize.desc: An immaculate, sharp silver sword that can slice through armor like moonlight flowing through the empty night. According to legend, it is a divine blade, blessed by the first Moonchanter herself.

customize.name: Sacrificer's Staff
customize.desc: A silver-white polearm, pure and completely without blemish. Legend has it that it was used by the Archpriestesses of Hyperborea in ages past to guide their flock of Frostmoon Scions.

customize.text: Silvermoon Hall

To the west of Hiisi Island, hidden from human view within the cliff, lies the refuge of the Moon Maiden,
the Silvermoon Hall. When Columbina left the Fatui and returned from Snezhnograd to Hiisi Island, she hid in the Silvermoon Hall, and only Lauma, the Moonchanter, knew of her presence. They first met shortly after the fall of the Ancient Moon Remnants, and Lauma asked the goddess what the Frostmoon Scions meant to her and why she had left. When Kuutar was born, before she could comprehend what was happening, the Frostmoon Scions began calling her their "goddess," and she had no reason to refuse. Like an infant accidentally swapped, she embraced their faith, and they, in turn, embraced her. But the feeling that something was missing only fueled their greed and doubt. They began asking her to forge weapons for them, drive out their enemies, expand their lands, heal their wounds, and grant them strength. They prayed for everything, and Kuutar fulfilled their will until the day came when she could no longer answer, having lost her strength. The Moon Goddess knew that back then, the Frostmoon Scions cared more about their own beliefs than about the truth itself. Her true home lay beyond the borders of the false sky, and so, realizing that the Frostmoon Scions had not become her true "home," she left Hiisi Island and journeyed north. Several centuries later, when the Frostmoon Scions had changed and were able to accept Columbina for who she was, rather than as a goddess, she opened the Silvermoon Hall to the eyes of people.

When the Rächer of Solnari first attacked Nod-Krai and attacked the Traveler, Ratnik Flins, and Columbina's best friend, Harbinger Sandrone, the Moon Goddess transported them to her chamber to protect them from the attack. It was there that Columbina received her true name. Since "Kuutar" was given to her by the Frostmoon Scions, and "Columbina" was a Fatui codename, the Moon Goddess had no name to keep her in Teyvat. When she lost all her powers due to Teyvat's rejection and disappeared, her friends set out to search for her true name, but even after visiting the ancient sanctuary of Hyperborea, they found nothing. They then decided to give her a new name that would anchor her in Teyvat, and they named her Columbina. The Moon Goddess herself added the name "Hyposelenia," meaning "born beneath the moon" or "born beneath this world." When Columbina was caught in the moon's reflection, her friend Sandrone went to the Silvermoon Hall. And although she understood that the Moon Goddess would not be there, hope still glimmered within her. After the Moon Goddess returned, Sandrone would visit her in the Silvermoon Hall for tea.

After the Frost Moon entered the borders of Teyvat's false sky, Columbina was finally able to return home. During her exploration, she encountered an unusual black kuuhenki. It was very weak, and the other kuuhenki allowed themselves to be consumed by it to give it strength. Columbina was worried about the kuuhenki, so she brought it to the Silvermoon Hall to keep it away from its kin until it regained its strength. When the black kuuhenki woke up, she didn't know who she was, but she remembered that her mission lay on the Frost Moon, so she tried her best to get there, even tricking the Traveler and Paimon into using the ancient dragon ship and going to the moon.

Columbina often spends her time in the Silvermoon Hall, playing with her kuuhenki familiars, and sometimes the Traveler and Paimon join them. Once, one of the kuuhenki, Maalaus, wanted to paint but couldn't mix the paints, so the Traveler shared with her the paint ingredients they had found during an adventure. Later, Columbina promised Maalaus to organize an exhibition of her paintings on the Frost Moon. The kuuhenki love music, so they often perform for the Moon Goddess, who sings along with them. And when a kuuhenki's lyre broke, Columbina would ask the animals or kuuhenki to discreetly carry the broken items to the house of Aino, the owner of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftsshop, so she could fix them. Aino, seeing the lyre mysteriously appear on her doorstep each time and then disappear, became frightened and didn't want to repair it. Then the Traveler and Paimon had to tell her about their mysterious friend, who couldn't show herself to people, and Aino agreed to repair the lyre. Moreover, the Traveler sometimes plays music from all over the world on the lyre for the kuuhenki. Sometimes the kuuhenki decorate the Silvermoon Hall with beautiful stones, and sometimes they play guessing games, cups, or moon chess. Sometimes during games, the kuuhenki remove the Moon Goddess's blindfold. One day, they didn't have enough stones for a drawing, so Columbina, the Traveler, and Paimon set out to find them, and along the way, they encountered a lost girl from the Frostmoon Scions. To hide the Moon Maiden's presence, she constructed a path of ore for the girl, directing her to the Frostmoon Enclave.

As Columbina had spent many years alone, she rarely sampled the food and drink of ordinary people. After meeting the Traveler, she often asked them to prepare various drinks from the tavern. The coffee drink seemed too bitter to her, but she remembered how Sandrone often drank it. The tea drink reminded her of the times she lived with the Frostmoon Scions. Every time she passed their houses, the subtle aroma of herbs, fresh mint leaves, spices, and dried herbs wafted through the windows. But the Moon Goddess never got a chance to taste it, because when a "goddess" comes asking for tea, no one dares offer her "simple tea" prepared for themselves. She also liked adding milk to her tea, as is customary in Mondstadt. The juice-based drink seemed tasteless to her. There was a time when Columbina couldn't understand why people experienced such joy during the harvest, but one day she reached out to touch a ripe fruit hanging on a branch. She sensed its vitality, and with each bite, she felt the refreshing sweetness wash over her in waves, like cool white foam. Therefore, she prefers fresh fruit, which allows her to see what she took from this world exactly as it was, and reminds her of her responsibilities to the world in return. When the Frostmoon Scions were preparing a surprise for Columbina and sculpting wings for the statue of the Moon Goddess, Lauma told her not to go outside, and especially to avoid the Frostmoon Scions. Columbina questioned the animals who brought her food, but Lauma ordered them to remain silent, and they complied. She suspected that the Frostmoon Scions were preparing something for her, but remained in the chambers so as not to disturb them with her curiosity.

customize.desc:
The Wild Hunt vanishes, chaos subsides, and the boughs of the Verdant Crest fill out quietly with life.

The Moon-Prayer Night, the night when the moon draws closest to Teyvat, is drawing near.

For a land and people long fractured, there is no better balm than a delightful night of celebration.

So why don't you and I step out together into this night of joy and laughter, amidst the blooming flowers bathed in the light of the moon?

customize.name: Moonfall Silver
customize.desc:
A silver crystal as pure and pristine as moonlight. It possesses almost perfect elemental affinity.
In the legacy of the Frostmoon Scions, these crystals were born five hundred years ago alongside the Moon Maiden, and were believed by the Moonchanter at the time to be a gift from the moon, hence the name "Moonfall Silver". However, in older documents written by Snezhnayan chroniclers, the descendants of the golden realm were already using secret silver woven by the Frostmoon thousands of years in the past. The threads that connect these two tales are unclear — the only certain thing is that these crystals make excellent elemental conductors in the eyes of Nod-Krai's craftspeople.

customize.name: Frostlamp Flower
customize.desc:
A flower that resembles a candle lamp, commonly found near water. It emits a cold, simple aroma that has a calming effect.
The contrasting colors of its stamen and stem are thought to symbolize the two different types of kuuvahki, yet despite this symbolism, it is one of the few rare plants that are immune to kuuvahki's influence. As a result, the Frostmoon Scions sometimes regard it as a symbol of faithlessness and apostasy.
It is said that this strangely shaped flower first appeared at the end of the dark calamity five hundred years ago, but this claim has never been rigorously verified.

customize.text: Materials & Ingredients

customize.name: Rainbowdrop Crystal
customize.desc:
A crystal that gives off an iridescent glow. Exceptionally tough and malleable, it has been regarded by Snezhnayan craftspeople as the best forging material since ancient times.
It is believed that when the moon's chariot was shattered, its blood-stained axle-tip fell into the earthly realm beneath the moon, transforming into an iridescent crystal. From that day on, the people of this land no longer worshipped the dead gods. The survivors who knew what the monarchs of the night died for, however, still futilely sing those long-forgotten names.

customize.name: Nocturnal Blossom
customize.desc:
A flower in two entwined colors with a strong affinity for kuuvahki. Its light fragrance and conspicuous color have made it an excellent natural dye.
Its contrasting colors are thought to symbolize the two different types of kuuvahki, so the followers of the Frostmoon Scions sometimes regard it as the Moon Maiden's blessing.
It is said that this strangely shaped flower first appeared decades after the dark calamity ended five hundred years ago, a claim widely reflected in the verses of the Frostmoon Scions, though it has never been rigorously verified.

customize.name: Icy Pebble
customize.desc:
A pebble commonly found on Nod-Krai's coasts, characterized by a naturally occurring hollow. Touching it sends a faint chill through your finger.
According to ancient legends, the hollows in these pebbles were once shelters revealed to the fae by the Frost Moon — gateways to the ethereal. In another story popular in Nasha Town, the legendary thief, Reed Miller, was surrounded when a runestone given to him by a holy lady of the Frost Moon as a token of her love allowed him to conceal himself and escape his pursuers. Naturally, the Frostmoon Scions vehemently reject this claim, as these pebbles do not display any such magical properties.

customize.name: Lakkaberry
customize.desc:
A fruit as white as pearl that tastes refreshingly sweet.
In the legends of the Frostmoon Scions, these fruits, like kuuhenki, are a gift from the Moon Maiden, a sacred symbol blessed by the new moon. Therefore, sharing and eating delicious Lakkaberries is also a form of worshipping Kuutar.
Even when not associated with the divine, their plumpness and sweetness alone are enough to awaken one's appetite.

customize.name: Radiant Antler
customize.desc:
A fragment of a defeated Frostnight Herra's majestic antlers. Light and razor-sharp, it requires no sharpening to help it slice through metal armor with ease.
According to ancient tales, these beautiful, proud creatures were created by the first emissary. When Elysium fell, they made a pact with the mistress of the Frost Moon, vowing to use the primal light bestowed by the Frost Moon to cleanse the mortal world's defilement until the patron of old could return once more. Today, these legends' origins are long lost, and their veracity is impossible to prove. Yet the creatures that once walked with the light continue to watch over this land from the shadows, through the long frozen nights and withering black tide alike — none of which could cause their forms to vanish from this world.

desc.text:
Dear Miss Aila,
I am truly sorry that I was unable to stop Miss Alia in that moment. Yet, it was through her noble sacrifice that we ultimately thwarted Rotwang and prevented the loss of countless lives. Now, I finally understand why she pretended to be my close companion. I hope to speak with you about this in greater detail when next we meet — though perhaps, by then, you will already know more about all this than I.
I shall not presume to judge, nor shall I attempt to alter your opinion of her. But I ask, if nothing else, that you allow me to honor Miss Alia's final wishes by sharing her words with you. She asked that I render all possible support to you (which I surely will. You are my benefactor, after all), and that — I relay this only as she spoke it — she hoped that you would go on to live a life of happiness and freedom.
As for the Arrow of Terpikeraunas you mentioned in your last letter, if it truly holds the power to dispel the pitch-black calamity, and if you are willing to share it with such selflessness, then on behalf of the people of Nod-Krai, please accept my deepest gratitude. Should, as you foresee, Rotwang indeed rise again from the pitch-black filth, then our successors — an order I am considering naming the "Lightkeepers," in honor of the flame you have kindled — will stand ready to vanquish the threat once more, armed with the technology you have so generously gifted us.
We can speak of the details in person whenever you are free. I understand all too well that, after Lovia's passing, the Frostmoon Scions have been left with countless matters demanding your attention.
Yours sincerely,
Solovei

...I told a lie, just like Lovia did, and just like my sister did. I said no when Mr. Solovei asked me if I felt any hate.
...But how can I put the hatred in my heart into words? How would someone as kind and sincere as he is ever understand such horrifying malice?
...No. I cannot think this way, and no one needs to know. Mr. Solovei does not need to be troubled with such trivial things. No one is obliged to bear the weight of another's suffering, which they have not experienced. And even if he truly were willing to listen, and even if his kindness were to move him to tears... what would it change? I would only end up bringing needless pain to another tender heart. In the past, the present, and the future, across the countless threads of fate that Lovia once let me glimpse by mistake, the only ones who shed tears for the misfortunes of others are kind souls who ought to be smiling instead. And since the sublunary sphere has always been one where good is repaid with cruelty, the least I could do is spare him a sorrow that does him no good.
...Once upon a time, I despised lies. Yet now, I find myself speaking them with keen intent. Maybe the [...] of the past dozen years or so has been punishment for this very moment...
...But that does not matter anymore. From the noble lady of Salt to the scions of Gurabad's jinni, there have been plenty of instances where the innocent have suffered the gravest of punishments, let alone a sinner as steeped in [...] as I am. If the silvery-white thread has already found its way around my neck, I may as well bear the weight of still more unforgivable sins by myself so that the children who remain untainted may be spared...
...What was born of the Frost Moon must return to it. All the walls, towers, fortresses, and temples must be torn down, save for the great pillar raised here by the Dragonborn, that is, the sacred sanctuary where our ancestors found refuge. Prolonged isolation and seclusion serve only to nourish fleeting ambitions and hollow delusions. Let it be reverence for nature, kindness toward outlanders, and those virtues in which none believe, and not the pride of the dead, which sets our threads apart from theirs. Only then will there never again be another Lovia... or another me.
...Decades from now, a new moon goddess will be born... Oh, the irony of it! Lovia's long and desperate quest was, in the end, for nothing. Even if [...] had borne the sacred heir as foretold, and not the man who abducted my sister... The one who should have been our sovereign would only have created even greater chaos in Snezhnaya. The birth of the new moon had nothing to do with anything she did. She could not even foresee the coming of that maiden, and nor did she know that the holy throne had never truly been broken...
...I do not know if I will live to see that moment, for my own thread is hidden from my sight. But I pray that I will not. Those tainted by sin do not deserve to witness the moon's pure light...
...In any case, people must come to believe that the new moon takes delight only in kindness, friendship, and mutual aid — that no other prayer or sacrifice will ever please our goddess. This is what they must believe, because if they do not, then no matter how noble the ideal, it will only wither and fade into the filth that lies beneath the moon...
...The threads of the gods are too bright for me to follow, and I cannot see where she is headed. But at the very least, the Frostmoon Scions, who have been redeemed in her name, must ensure that the power of choice remains hers alone. No one should ever seek repayment or reward from her, and she must never be molded into the "perfect deity" others wish her to become...
...Daughter of the Frost Moon, maiden of the new moon... May she one day behold the dream of true happiness... and may the Frost Moon never forgive my sins, for I have cursed her name more times than I can count.

To the most holy and venerable Lady Lovia:
I pen this letter to account for the tragic event that transpired earlier. You asked that I send people to welcome the holy lady, and I did exactly as you instructed. But that poor girl — alas for her great beauty! — failed to grasp the kindness behind your gesture, and seized by some terrible impulse, she took her own life on the spot. For this terrible, irreparable loss, I can offer only my prayers. I pray that your compassionate goddess may ease your sorrow and keep your noble heart from breaking, despite the weight of this grief.
Regarding the "Sampo Mill" mentioned in your last letter, I am truly grateful for your openness and trust. Like you, I remain uninitiated in the true workings of this sacred relic. Yet on this matter, we are of one mind: We must find another way to rouse this ancient relic and forge a paradise, an Elysium of enduring prosperity for the people of Nod-Krai, especially your noble kin. From this moment on, I shall dedicate myself wholly to uncovering the secrets that lie within the relic.
As for the remaining matters, both more trivial and complex, I hope to discuss them at greater length with you soon. Until then, I ask that you accept these modest gifts as a small token of my regard and a gesture of sympathy for the loss that has touched your household. Please know that I hold your noble character in the highest esteem. Even at the court of His Majesty the Belyi Tsar, it is rare to encounter a lady of such uncommon foresight and deep devotion to the greater good as yourself, not to mention one who so willingly places the well-being of the nation and her people above personal sentiment. Our positions, interests, and aspirations are most closely aligned. As such, I greatly look forward to our future joint endeavors.
Your ever-steadfast friend and ally,
Rotwang

This decree was issued by Saredne, humble handmaiden of the Frost Moon and 13th Archpriestess since the fall of Hyperborea. It is not to be defied. In the name of the mistress of the Frost Moon, the ancient laws, once obscure and difficult to understand, are now set forth in clear and concise terms, lest the faithful falter or be led astray.
